lessons.title: Understanding Themes in Literature
lessons.lecture:
Hello and welcome to today’s lecture! My name is [insert name], and I’m excited to dive into the fascinating world of themes in literature with you today. Today, we will focus on identifying themes in various genres of literature. This will enhance your analytical skills as a reader. Let’s get started by discussing what a theme is.

A theme in literature refers to the central idea or message that the author wants to convey through the text. It can often be expressed in a single word or a phrase, such as love, conflict, or courage. Themes are crucial because they help us make sense of the story and connect with the characters and their experiences. As a reader, being able to identify themes will deepen your understanding and appreciation of the literature you encounter.

Now, we will first explore themes in poetry vs. prose. [p] 
Poetry often expresses themes through emotions, imagery, and stylistic devices. The language in poetry tends to be more concentrated, which means that every word is chosen carefully to convey a rich meaning. For example, love is a common theme in poetry, and poets might explore it differently based on their personal experiences or societal norms.

lessons.summary: In today’s lecture, you learned about the importance of themes in literature, how themes are expressed differently in poetry and prose, and the process of analyzing character development to uncover deeper meanings. Understanding these aspects will allow you to engage more thoughtfully with a wide range of literary works in the future. You now have the tools to identify themes, whether they are apparent or subtle, and appreciate the layers of meaning that literature offers.
